parsed.headline: UAE prosecutor says Flydubai co-pilot used crash axe in attempted terrorist attack

pages.text: A United Arab Emirates prosecutor general stated on Saturday that the co-pilot of Flydubai flight FZ1073 used a crash axe to attempt a “terrorist attack” during an Israel-bound flight. Gen Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, the UAE prosecutor, told the state news agency WAM that investigations are ongoing to uncover the circumstances, motives, and related connections of the incident. The aircraft, which was carrying 182 people, plunged 16,625 feet in just over 30 seconds on September 30, 2026, before passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot's attempt to take control. The extreme descent resulted in part of the plane's rudder being ripped off. Following the incident, two other pilots in the cabin took control and landed the aircraft safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The Flydubai captain, an Indian national identified as Smit Machchhar, sustained wounds to his head, hands, and neck. Machchhar reported to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that he used his remaining energy to unlock the cockpit door, allowing others to enter, subdue the co-pilot, and stabilize the plane.

Media outlets have identified the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national. Reports from the Wall Street Journal and the Associated Press indicate that al-Hammami had previously been barred from flying by Oman due to concerns regarding extremist or radical ideological views. Following that ban, he was reportedly moved to an administrative role at Oman Air before being hired by the UAE-based Flydubai. It remains unclear to what extent he was vetted during the Flydubai hiring process. While investigators had previously sought to determine how a weapon might have been smuggled onboard, Gen Hamad Saif al-Shamsi noted that the crash axe is an implement typically kept inside the cockpit for emergencies, such as fires or crashes. Security agencies from four regional countries, including Israel, are working to establish whether the suspect acted as a “lone wolf” or had connections to extremist groups, with assistance from the United States and other Western governments. On October 2, 2026, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the co-pilot had undergone “Islamist radicalization,” though he provided no evidence.

parsed.headline: Price of 12kg LPG cylinder increases by Tk 252 in Bangladesh

pages.text: The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) announced on October 4, 2026, that the consumer price for private-sector liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has increased. The price of the most widely used 12kg LPG cylinder rose by Tk 252, moving from Tk 1,585 to Tk 1,837. This represents a price increase of Tk 21 per kilogramme. The new pricing was scheduled to take effect at 6:00 pm on October 4, 2026. This follows a price decrease of Tk 13 during the previous month.

The price adjustment follows a period of fluctuation in the international market. While prices declined for two consecutive months in June and July following a ceasefire, a significant surge occurred this month. Previously, in April, the country saw its highest-ever increase in LPG prices, when the 12kg cylinder price rose by Tk 387 at the beginning of the month and by an additional Tk 212 on 19 April. BERC noted that LPG cylinders of various sizes remain available in the market, though allegations have surfaced that 12kg cylinders are being sold at Tk 500 to Tk 800 above the official price due to market supply remaining below demand for the past three weeks.

parsed.headline: Former Ghanaian Ambassador congratulates New Patriotic Party leaders on election results

pages.text: Edward Boateng, the former Ghanaian Ambassador to China, has congratulated John Boadu and Justin Frimpong Kodua following their election and re-election, respectively, as National Chairman and General Secretary of the New Patriotic Party (NPP). Following the NPP’s National Delegates Conference, Mr. Boateng stated that the results carry a responsibility for both leaders to rebuild the party, strengthen its structures, and unite members ahead of the 2028 general elections. He urged the new National Chairman to use his mandate to promote reconciliation and bring together members who supported different candidates during the internal elections. Mr. Boateng noted that Mr. Kodua became the first person since Dan Botwe to be elected as General Secretary for a second consecutive term, and stated that Mr. Kodua must work with Chairman Boadu to ensure party structures function effectively from the polling station to the national level.

parsed.headline: Amazon rainforest policy future tied to Brazilian presidential election

pages.text: Brazil’s upcoming presidential election may determine the future of the Amazon rainforest, which accounts for approximately 60% of the ecosystem. Experts have warned that a victory for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, could reverse deforestation-control policies that were restored by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. During the presidency of Jair Bolsonaro, Amazon deforestation increased by about 60%. In 2023, President Lula reinstated an anti-deforestation plan that reduced deforestation by 45%. Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to end illegal deforestation by 2029, though he has not provided details on how this goal would be achieved. Concerns persist regarding the potential weakening of environmental protections.

parsed.headline: More than 1,200 Colorado students earn climate literacy seal

pages.text: More than 1,200 students in Colorado have earned a climate literacy seal, a statewide initiative that combines climate-focused coursework with community service. Since Colorado lawmakers approved the seal in 2024, 26 of the state’s 179 school districts have adopted the program, according to the education non-profit Lyra Colorado. To earn the endorsement for their high school diplomas and transcripts, students must complete at least two advanced courses covering Earth’s climate systems and an approved project addressing a local climate issue. Anthony Muñoz, a student at Vista Academy, completed a capstone project by building an “ozone garden” using native plants to detect ground-level ozone pollution. For this project, Muñoz worked with climate scientists from the National Center for Atmospheric Research in Boulder to collect data on air quality and the impact of milkweed on monarch butterfly migration. The model for the seal is expanding to other states; Maine adopted a similar seal earlier this year, and California recently signed a bill to establish one for its graduates. Youth coalitions have also pursued the policy in Hawaii and Minnesota.

parsed.headline: Toronto Fire Services launches Fire Prevention Week 2026 with focus on lithium-ion battery safety

pages.text: Toronto Fire Services has launched Fire Prevention Week 2026, scheduled to take place from Sunday, October 4 to October 10, 2026. According to a statement from the City of Toronto, the campaign theme is “Safe Charging Is a Superpower,” which focuses on charging habits intended to prevent lithium-ion battery fires in homes and communities. Lithium-ion batteries are used in various daily devices, including smartphones, tablets, e-bikes, e-scooters, and other portable electronics. While these batteries are generally safe when used properly, Toronto Fire Services notes that damaged, defective, or improperly charged batteries can pose a serious fire risk. Jim Jessop, Fire Chief of Toronto Fire Services, stated that safe charging involves using approved equipment and following manufacturer instructions, such as using approved chargers, cords, and batteries, avoiding tampering with or modifying devices, and replacing any damaged or defective charging equipment.

parsed.headline: Toronto Fire Services launches Fire Prevention Week 2026 focusing on safe charging

pages.text: Toronto Fire Services is encouraging residents to prioritize fire safety during Fire Prevention Week 2026, which is scheduled to take place from Sunday, October 4 to October 3, 2026. The theme for this year is “Safe Charging Is a Superpower,” a campaign centered on charging habits intended to help prevent lithium-ion battery fires in homes and communities. Lithium-ion batteries are used in various daily devices, including smartphones, tablets, e-bikes, e-scooters, and other portable electronics. While generally safe when used properly, Toronto Fire Services notes that damaged, defective, or improperly charged batteries can pose a serious fire risk. Jim Jessop, Fire Chief of Toronto Fire Services, stated that safe charging involves using approved equipment and following manufacturer instructions, such as using approved chargers, cords, and batteries, avoiding tampering with or modifying devices, and replacing any damaged or defective charging equipment.

parsed.headline: Latvia's United List party secures largest parliamentary election victory since independence

pages.text: In Latvia's parliamentary election, the centrist United List party led by Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs secured a historic victory, appearing to win the largest share of votes since the country regained independence from the Soviet Union in 1991. Preliminary results indicated that with 97% to 99.9% of ballots counted, the United List earned approximately 35.3% to 35.4% of the vote, granting the party 42 of the 100 seats in the Saeima. The result places Kulbergs, a 47-year-old businessman and amateur rally driver, in a position to form a pro-Ukraine coalition. Kulbergs, who assumed office in May after a previous coalition collapsed following incidents involving stray Ukrainian military drones, stated on the night of October 3, 2026, that he would not cooperate with pro-Russian parties and specifically ruled out a coalition with the populist Latvia First party. Political scientist Roberts Kits noted that the United List could potentially secure a parliamentary majority by partnering with either the left-leaning Progressives or the nationalist National Alliance. The election, which involved 14 parties contesting 100 seats via a proportional system, was shaped by concerns regarding national security and rising living costs. While most parties support high military spending and aid to Kyiv, the Sovereign Power party opposed military aid to Ukraine and increased defense spending, appearing set to finish third. An exit poll placed the populist Latvia First party in second place with 11.3%, nearly double its 2022 share. Both populist parties were noted as benefiting from shifts in voting patterns among Latvia's ethnic Russian-speaking minority.

uncertainties: The exact final percentage of the vote and total seat count are subject to the completion of the count, with reports citing between 97% and 99.9% processed.

parsed.headline: BGMEA president urges Pakistan to increase imports from Bangladesh to address trade imbalance

pages.text: Mahmud Hasan Khan, President of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), has urged Pakistan to increase its imports of Bangladeshi products to address an existing trade imbalance. During a bilateral meeting in Uttara, Dhaka, Khan specifically identified high-quality jute yarn and life-saving pharmaceuticals as key sectors for increased exports to Pakistan. He noted that while Bangladesh imports significant volumes of essential raw materials, such as chemicals and dyes for the ready-made garment (RMG) sector, from Pakistan, Bangladeshi exports to Pakistan remain disproportionately low. The meeting included Pakistani High Commissioner to Bangladesh Imran Haidar and took place on a Sunday, though the specific calendar date was not established by the report from The Financial Express Bangladesh. To strengthen economic cooperation, Khan also called for the modernization of logistics to address excessive time required for direct maritime transportation.

In response to the proposals, High Commissioner Imran Haidar expressed interest and assured BGMEA leadership that measures would be taken to boost two-way trade. Haidar suggested the exchange of high-level business delegations to explore market opportunities, stating that the High Commission would organize Business-to-Business (B2B) meetings and matchmaking sessions with Pakistani importers, brands, and trade bodies if a Bangladeshi delegation visits. Discussions also included potential market access strategies, such as formulating a bilateral special Free Trade Agreement (FTA) mechanism to sustain trade flows following Bangladesh's graduation from LDC status under SAFTA. Additionally, the parties discussed institutional development, including technology transfer and student exchange programs between the BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT) and Pakistani textile institutes.

parsed.headline: Iran says Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until seven conditions are met

pages.text: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated on Sunday that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions, outlined in an interim understanding reached with the United States last June, are fulfilled. Ghalibaf, speaking via the state-linked news agency Nournews, said the decision follows Tehran receiving a U.S. response to its diplomatic proposal. He noted that Washington recently submitted new proposals through a mediator, despite what he described as differences between those proposals and public statements. Ghalibaf stated that Tehran would no longer accept stalling or the imposition of unilateral demands, asserting that the resumption of navigation through the strait is tied to the fulfillment of conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum of understanding. He added that Iran would both fight and negotiate and is prepared to confront the U.S. with new surprises on the military battlefield. Last week, U.S. President Donald Trump ruled out an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait, which is used to ship one-fifth of global oil and natural gas during peacetime.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told foreign ambassadors and diplomats in Tehran that Iran has clearly explained its conditions for reopening the waterway and hopes Washington will choose diplomacy. Araghchi stated that Iran is serious about finding diplomatic solutions but warned that if the U.S. takes military action again, Iran is more prepared than before and will take necessary action to defend itself. Additionally, Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei noted that Tehran used the United Nations General Assembly platform last month to present its position regarding the end of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran.

parsed.headline: US Vice-President JD Vance aligns with Make America Healthy Again movement

pages.text: US Vice-President JD Vance, a widely considered Republican frontrunner for the 2028 presidential election, is aligning himself with the Make America Healthy Again (Maha) movement, according to reporting by The Guardian World. At a Maha summit in Washington, DC, on September 29, 2026, Vance engaged with Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and leader of Maha, discussing topics such as memes and the “carnivore” diet. Vance has positioned himself as the inheritor of the Make America Great Again (Maga) movement, and his attachment to Maha signals an overlap between the two movements as the administration's popularity declines amid rising prices and the war in Iran. Art Caplan, professor emeritus at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine, noted that Vance underlined the politics being stirred up by Maha during the event. While Kennedy spoke regarding the inefficiencies of the US health system compared to European universal healthcare, Vance highlighted his role leading an anti-fraud task force. Vance claimed the task force has identified close to $250bn in fraud within Medicaid, Medicare, and the Affordable Care Act marketplace, alleging that undocumented immigrants are receiving benefits. The administration has released few details regarding why specific individuals were unenrolled from these programs or the nature of the alleged fraud, and there is no documentation currently available to support the claim that undocumented people are receiving Medicare benefits.
